Support (Likelihood) Intervals From A Likelihood Function

Source: R/curve_likelihood.R
curve_support.Rd

Computes likelihood/support intervals – the set of parameter values whose relative likelihood exceeds \(1/k\) – from any concurve likelihood dataframe, using monotone interpolation on each shoulder of the function rather than snapping to grid points.

curve_support(data, cutoffs = c(6.83, 8, 32))

Arguments

data

The likelihood dataframe produced by curve_lik(), as_curve_lik(), curve_lik_glm(), or curve_lik_exact().

cutoffs

A numeric vector of \(k\) values. The default c(6.83, 8, 32).

Value

A data frame with one row per cutoff: k, the implied relative-likelihood threshold, the interval limits, and the MLE.

Details

The conventional cutoffs are \(1/6.83\) (which corresponds to the 95\ \(\exp(-\chi^2_{1,0.95}/2)\)), and Royall's \(1/8\) and \(1/32\) benchmarks for "fairly strong" and "strong" evidence.

References

Royall R. Statistical Evidence: A Likelihood Paradigm. Chapman & Hall/CRC; 1997.

See also

as_curve_lik() curve_lik_glm() curve_lik_exact()

Examples

p <- seq(0.001, 0.999, length.out = 2000)
lik <- as_curve_lik(p, 8 * log(p) + 12 * log(1 - p))
curve_support(lik[[1]])
#>       k support.level lower.limit upper.limit       mle
#> 1  6.83     0.1464129   0.2070813   0.6170994 0.4000001
#> 2  8.00     0.1250000   0.2005429   0.6255044 0.4000001
#> 3 32.00     0.0312500   0.1552594   0.6863991 0.4000001
